characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy aims to demonstrate the viability of alternative authentication methods for Denmark's digital identity infrastructure. By developing technical demonstrators, this lever seeks to provide concrete evidence that supports policy advocacy and procurement influence. Key success metrics include the completion of demonstrators, increased policy traction by 15%, and enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations, ultimately leading to a more resilient digital identity framework.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes strongly with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as the technical evidence generated can significantly bolster policy proposals. Additionally, it enhances the Coalition Building Strategy by providing tangible results that attract more stakeholders to the cause.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: However, the Technical Feasibility Strategy may conflict with the Procurement Influence Strategy, as a focus on specific technical solutions could limit the flexibility needed in procurement documents. It may also constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if the demonstrators do not align with the broader coalition's interests.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy focuses on shaping procurement processes and influencing the requirements for Denmark's digital identity systems. By submitting policy proposals and engaging with stakeholders, this lever aims to increase the likelihood of adopting platform-neutral standards by 20%. Success metrics include the number of proposals submitted and the degree of influence on AltID requirements, ultimately fostering a more resilient digital identity infrastructure.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy works synergistically with the Coalition Building Strategy, as a strong coalition can amplify advocacy efforts. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy, as concrete technical evidence can strengthen policy arguments and increase their acceptance.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The Policy Advocacy Strategy may conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy if the advocacy focus on continuity and supplier concentration risks alienates potential allies who prioritize privacy concerns. Additionally, it may constrain the Procurement Influence Strategy if it becomes too narrowly focused on specific arguments.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy aims to strengthen stakeholder engagement and advocacy for platform neutrality in Denmark's digital identity infrastructure. By forming a diverse coalition, this lever seeks to enhance the advocacy position by 30% in procurement discussions. Key success metrics include the number of stakeholders engaged and the breadth of support achieved, ultimately increasing political pressure for platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as a robust coalition can amplify advocacy efforts and increase the likelihood of influencing policy. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy, as demonstrators can attract more stakeholders to the coalition.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: However, the Coalition Building Strategy may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if the coalition's interests diverge from the technical focus of the demonstrators. It may also constrain the Procurement Influence Strategy if conflicting priorities within the coalition lead to fragmented advocacy efforts.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy aims to drive the adoption of platform-neutral language in procurement documents for Denmark's digital identity systems. By advocating for specific requirements and supplier diversity, this lever seeks to reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Key success metrics include the inclusion of platform-neutral language in procurement documents and the speed of scaling through mandated diversity, ultimately fostering a more resilient digital identity framework.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as successful advocacy can lead to more favorable procurement language. It also benefits from the Coalition Building Strategy, as a strong coalition can support procurement efforts and enhance the push for platform neutrality.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: However, the Procurement Influence Strategy may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if the focus on specific procurement language limits the flexibility needed for technical solutions. It may also constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if the procurement focus alienates stakeholders who prioritize other aspects of digital identity.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy focuses on influencing European standards related to digital identity, particularly in alignment with the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. By providing input to relevant EU bodies, this lever aims to increase alignment with EU requirements by 10% and enhance interoperability across Europe. Key success metrics include the number of engagements with EU bodies and the degree of influence on standards, ultimately fostering a more cohesive digital identity landscape.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy synergizes with the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as aligning with EU standards can strengthen national advocacy efforts. It also complements the Procurement Influence Strategy by ensuring that procurement documents align with broader European requirements, enhancing their credibility.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: However, the EU Standards Engagement Strategy may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if the focus on EU standards limits the exploration of innovative technical solutions. It may also constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if the emphasis on EU alignment alienates local stakeholders who prioritize national concerns.
